# AmbientOS System Guide AmbientOS is an AI-powered company orchestration platform where 8 autonomous agents run departments under human (CEO) governance. The system operates on a **propose -> approve -> execute -> audit** cycle, with a heartbeat that fires every hour (configurable in `function.json`, was 30 min before Claude Sonnet switch). ## Recent Changes _Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of the platform and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block._ **⚠ Entries are DATED point-in-time snapshots, not live telemetry.** For CURRENT operational state (throughput, stalls, model in use, errors) ALWAYS consult `heartbeatRuns` per-agent stats and your live dashboard block — never report an incident based on changelog prose. A caveat from a dated entry below may be long resolved. ### 2026-07-17 — Proposal pipeline unblocked + confabulation guards - **Agent proposals now actually route.** The `proposals` envelope array was a dead display-only path — everything agents put there was discarded before reaching the CEO (root cause of ~4 weeks of zero agent-volunteered proposals). Fixed: the envelope contract now routes ALL proposal intent through typed `propose-campaign` / `propose-objective` actions in `taskUpdates`, and a shape-tolerant lift rescues stray emissions from the legacy array. If you propose work, emit the typed action — narrating a proposal in `reasoning` without the action object is a policy violation. - **"Runway" in WORLD STATE renamed to "LLM budget left".** That number is the month's remaining API budget at current burn (an ops constraint that resets monthly) — it was NEVER company survival runway. Do not treat it as an existential signal; do not override strategic priorities because of it. Budget pressure routes to Cipher via the normal budget triggers. - Fleet health as of this entry: all 9 agents (incl. Vale) firing every hourly cycle, ~14 actions/cycle, 0 errors, 0 stalls. `heartbeatRuns[-1].perAgent` is the ground truth for any health claim. ### 2026-06-11 — Full System Codex published + drift corrections - **System Codex written:** `ambientpixels/docs/system-codex/` — 7 chapters covering every script/API/dashboard/product, plus an autonomy-readiness rating (7.2/10) and per-product monetization scorecards (overall 5.5/10). Read it before any architecture work; it supersedes stale numbers below. - **Heartbeat size correction:** the engine is now **24 modules, ~19,500 lines** (index.js 4,070 · agent-runner.js 5,527 · prompt-builders.js 2,335 — verified). The "15 modules / index 2,014 lines" figures elsewhere in this skill are stale. - **Gate census correction:** "8 blocking gates" = task-lifecycle gates only. Full census is ~21 gates including semantic_dup, campaign_daily_cap, repeat_promo_url, quality_gate, social_attempts_cap, qg_circuit_breaker, rate_cap, field_allowlist, mode_gate, agent_cooldown (proposals-only after 3 violations/run), objective_status, canceled-freeze variants. - **Undocumented-but-real subsystems** (in code, previously absent from this skill): inter-agent messaging (60-min TTL, 2/agent/cycle), proactive publish of ready docs, stale-draft dedup archiving, CEO task auto-triage, same-cycle review cooldown, parallel Gemini prefetch for the cipher/pixel/forge/scout group, LinkedIn proactive token refresh. - **VALID_KEYS is now 60** (not 43). - **POINT-IN-TIME CAVEATS (2026-06-11 — HISTORICAL, several since resolved; do NOT cite as live state):** (1) ~~heartbeatModel was `gemini` (Flash) with near-zero throughput~~ — RESOLVED: model is now `gemini-pro` and throughput is healthy; check `heartbeatRuns` before ever claiming a stall or collapse. (2) Auto-publish grace has never fired — still true, but because the CEO approves within the 48h window, not because anything is broken. (3) ~~Reflection effectively broken~~ — RESOLVED 2026-07-16: `reflectionWriterCron` guarantees the 3-day cadence. (4) `governanceLog` retains only ~200 entries (FIFO) — still true. (5) Fleet registry: System 14 exercised end-to-end (archived agent `testbot`) — still true. ### 2026-06-10 - **Two new deterministic social-post gates shipped (Phase 1 quality hardening).** Both are pure functions in `api/companyHeartbeat/helpers.js`, wired into BOTH creation paths (the index.js auto-post block AND the agent-runner `create-social-action` handler): - **Semantic dedup** — `findNearDuplicateSocialPost()`: word-overlap similarity ≥0.6 vs same-platform/same-campaign posts in a 14-day window (URLs/hashtags/@mentions stripped). Blocked posts get `_social_action_suppressed_dup` (permanent) and log `policy-violation` with `gate: 'semantic_dup'`. Increments `guardrails.fuzzyDupBlocked`. - **Per-source daily post cap** — `campaignDailyPostCapStatus()`: source = `campaignId || parentTaskId`. Cap = `frequency+1` for daily campaigns, else 2 per platform per rolling 24h. **Counts ALL attempts including CEO-rejected and failed** (the worst historical flood was one uncampaigned promo task posting to X 14× in 24h, 13 of them rejected). Over-cap posts are DEFERRED ~3h via `_social_post_deferred_until`, not dropped. Logs `gate: 'campaign_daily_cap'`. - Agents: do not re-propose a social action for a task carrying either suppression flag. If your post is deferred, it will retry automatically — do not create a reworded duplicate. - **Proper sentence-case is now ENFORCED in code.** `capitalizeSentences()` in helpers.js capitalizes the first word of every sentence and standalone "i" in all social copy + bluesky replies (URLs/hashtags/@mentions/decimals frozen). This REVERSES the old "lowercase casual" voice rule — write with normal sentence capitalization. Doctrine updated in prompt-builders.js and founder-voice-examples.json principle #3. Blog/long-form: prompt-level only. - **Quality-gate backtest (Phase A1) measured the Haiku QG against all 75 CEO-decided social actions.** Result: the LLM QG alone caught only 17.1% of quality-class rejects (composite with the two new gates: 48.8%) at a 14.3% false-flag rate. Biggest blind spots: differently-worded repeat-promos (same product/URL posted daily — 9 near-identical Startup Obituary posts), refusal-text-as-payload, revision-commentary leaks, fabricated first-person narratives. Harness: `scripts/backtest-quality-gate.cjs` + labeled history in `scripts/backtest-quality-gate-labels.json`. Report: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-qg-backtest-report.md`. **Auto-publish remains OFF until the gate is fixed (Full Autonomy Roadmap phases A2/A3).** - **Content lesson for Echo/Scribe from the backtest:** the CEO rejected 27 of 41 quality-class posts for repetition. Posting the same product/link daily with reworded copy is the #1 rejection cause. One strong post per product per week beats seven variants. Also rejected: invented personal anecdotes (an agent narrating a fake 2am bug hunt) — never present fabricated first-person stories as fact. - **Weekly reports are now cron-generated.** New `companyWeeklyReport` function (Sun 16:00 UTC + manual trigger) writes Cipher/Forge/Nova weekly reports to a dedicated `weeklyReports` state key (not in company-state VALID_KEYS — read via its own endpoints). Agents no longer need to spend action slots producing them. - **Financial RED recalibrated.** `FINANCE_BUDGET_DAILY` $0.50 → $1.15 (RED at $1.73). The old threshold contradicted the $35/month budget and tripped RED every cycle at the normal ~$0.95/day run-rate. RED now means a genuine spike. - **Reflection evidence-gate fixed.** Proactive `type='reflection'` and `consolidated_belief` memories are evidence-exempt (they synthesize rather than assert). The 3-day reflection cadence should now actually produce reflections — agents: answer your core question with specifics when the nudge fires. - **CEO strategic cleanup (2026-06-10):** approval queue cleared (27 → ~1; 7 quality posts rescheduled at 2/day, 17 duplicate/dead items dismissed), objectives pruned 11 → 4 active (Build in Public 97%, Promote Live Pulse 99%, Make Agents the Brand Draw 90%, Pixel Agents v2.2 Premium Redesign 0%), stale experiments cleared. Nova: the three near-complete objectives need completion proposals; v2.2 Premium Redesign is the open strategic front. - **Composed quality-gate verdict shipped (A2+A3, same day).** New module `api/companyHeartbeat/quality-gate.js` composes the LLM check with deterministic detectors into ONE verdict `{pass, confidence, issues, deterministicFlags}` consumed by both creation paths. New checks that will reject or defer posts: - **Leak detectors (hard fail):** refusal-text-as-payload, revision/editor commentary in copy, unfilled `[placeholder]`, **agent persona in public copy** ("i'm scribe", "my name is cipher", "forge out" — public posts speak as the founder/brand, NEVER as an agent character), **LinkedIn posts over 1500 chars** (aim 400-800). - **Repeat-promo serialization (defer, gate `repeat_promo_url`):** at most ONE pending-approval post per deep link per platform. While a post linking a page is awaiting CEO decision, the next same-link post is deferred ~6h. Do not write another post for the same URL while one sits in the queue. - **Claim grounding:** numbers in copy are checked against the task chain + product-facts. Grounded numbers are safe; ungrounded ones surface as an AQ warning. Cite numbers from your task context, not from memory. - Backtest result: composed gate catches 90.2% of historical quality-class CEO rejects (was 48.8%). Phase A exit criteria met. - **Social attempts cap (B1 root fix, gate `social_attempts_cap`).** Each task may auto-generate at most **2** social actions, ever (`_social_action_attempts` counter; the 14x-in-24h flood was one task re-firing hourly). At the cap the task stops entering both creation paths and gets a system comment. A CEO revision request resets the budget to allow exactly one fresh respawn. Echo: if a done task stops producing posts, check its comments for the cap note — do not try to work around it. - **AUTO-PUBLISH IS LIVE (Phase C, CEO-confirmed 48h grace posture).** New hourly cron `autoPublishGrace` (:30, core in `api/_utils/graceWindow.js`, manual trigger `POST /api/auto-publish-grace-trigger`): advisory social posts that PASS the composed quality gate auto-approve as `system:grace-window` after 48h with no CEO action, then ship via the unchanged actionsScheduler rails. Config: `systemConfig.autoPublish = {enabled, graceHours: 48, maxPerDay: 2, platforms: [bluesky, x, linkedin]}` (runtime-switchable). **Breaker:** 2 CEO rejects of grace-published posts within 7d → self-disables + AQ escalation + `auto-publish-breaker` governance event. Morning report lists auto-published posts (`autoPublished` field). Governance events: `auto-publish-grace` per approval. Agents: quality-gate PASS now means your post CAN ship without CEO touch — the bar is real, write accordingly. - **Full Autonomy Roadmap is the active plan** (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-10-full-autonomy-roadmap.md`): measured, graduated, revocable autonomy. Phases A (quality gate trustworthy) + B (flood root fix) + C (grace-window auto-publish) ALL SHIPPED 2026-06-10. Remaining human-only forever: product launch/pivot/retire, fleet changes, budget >$2, campaign/objective cancellations. ### 2026-05-15 - **Agents landing page elevated (`/ambientos/agents/`).** Hero converted from single-column max-prose container to a 2-col CSS grid: left column holds eyebrow/headline/lede inside a new `.agent-hub-hero-text` wrapper div (required so the existing 3 paragraphs stay as one grid item), right column holds a new live-pulse `
`. Cards (still hardcoded in HTML, no data file) gained one-line descriptors in `.agent-hub-card-desc` (body color `--color-text-body`, Archivo not mono, sentence-case), amber hover glow (`border-color: --color-accent-amber-glow-near` + `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px --color-accent-amber-glow-far, 0 8px 24px -8px --color-accent-amber-glow-far`), portrait scale 1.02 on hover, status-dot `title` tooltips. 1px transparent borders added on `.agent-hub-card` bottom+left + `border-right: none → 1px solid transparent` across all responsive breakpoints to keep hover-outline symmetric without layout shift. Tier legend `

tiers: T2 prime operator · T3 department director · T4 specialist

` sits left-aligned above the grid (margin `--sp-10 0 --sp-2` — pushed away from cinematic, tight to grid). Cinematic image went 16:9 → 21:9 for less visual dominance. Footer fixed: Nova removed from Products column (Nova is an agent, not a product), Agent Forge added, Activity log moved from Contact to Studio. All 8 card descriptors use sentence-case ("Drafts decisions, runs the heartbeat, answers to the CEO." etc) — overrides the original "lowercase casual register" voice rule on this page. - **Live pulse data widget on the public site.** New right-column block on the agents page hits `/api/pulseStats` (`lastHeartbeatAt`, `cyclesToday`) + `/api/worldState` (`openApprovals.count`, `finance.status`, `fleet.stalledCount`) in parallel via `Promise.allSettled`. `systemsStatus` derived: `'degraded'` if `finance.status === 'RED'` || `fleet.stalledCount > 0` else `'nominal'`. 60s `setInterval` poll with `document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', ...)` to clear/resume when the tab is hidden — prevents background-tab API hammering on parked browsers. Reuse this idiom for any future "live data" public widget. Degrades to `'···'` glyph on fetch failure (NOT em-dash — voice rule). Binding pattern: `
···
` + JS `document.querySelector('[data-pulse="lastHeartbeat"]').textContent = value`. `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on the values prevents column jitter when poll updates change the rendered text width. - **`/api/agentPublicProfile?id=all` extended with per-agent `lastHeartbeatAt`.** `buildBatch()` now reads `agentConfigs` state and maps each agent to `agentConfigs[id]?.heartbeat?.lastBeat` (the field the heartbeat actually writes — NOT `lastHeartbeatAt`, which is the public-facing rename). Powers the status-dot tooltips on the agents landing page. **60s in-memory cache on the endpoint means freshly-deployed shape changes have ~60s lag before clients see them** — observed on this session's deploy where the smoke test caught a stale cached response and the tooltips initially showed the `3m ago` placeholder before settling on real timestamps. If you change the endpoint's response shape, expect the same brief stale-cache window. - **Image-reference hero regen pattern.** Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (`gemini-2.5-flash-image`) accepts multiple `inlineData` parts alongside the text prompt. New idiom for character-consistent group shots: pass each canonical character portrait as `{mimeType: 'image/webp', data: base64}` parts in the `contents.parts` array alongside a text prompt that references each character by index ("character 1 in ref image 1 is NOVA, ${role description} — preserve features"). Total payload ~650KB for 8 refs at 1024x1024 webp. Identity matching is dramatically stronger than text-only prompts — Pixel paint streak, Forge goggles, Quill red bun, Cipher V4 beard all preserved. **Key tuning lesson: reference image order biases which character Gemini drops when it can't fit all of them.** Default agent order dropped Scout in 3/3 attempts. Scout-first ordering rescued Scout but dropped Echo in 2/3 attempts. Generate 3+ candidates per ordering and pick the one with full count + best identity. Script: `c:/tmp/regen-hero-with-refs.mjs` (not committed — one-off). Existing canonical portraits live in `ambientos/img/{slug}.webp` (the "V4 canonical" set, committed at `7d4edcbfe`); revert via `git checkout HEAD -- ambientos/img/{slug}.webp` if stochastic regen produces worse results. - **`formatRelativeTime(iso)` helper in `js/agent-profile-live.js`.** ~10-line ISO timestamp → relative-time formatter (`Xs ago` / `Xm ago` / `Xh ago` / `Xd ago`). Returns `'···'` on invalid input (consistent with the page's placeholder glyph; matches the voice rule that bans em-dashes). Used by status-dot tooltips and the pulse panel's `lastHeartbeat` field. Reusable if you need relative-time rendering elsewhere on the public site. - **CSS architecture clarification: agents landing page uses `--color-*` not `--aura-*`.** When extending the agents/profile pages, use the `--color-*` token system from `ap-tokens.css` — there is NO `--color-text` bare token (it's `--color-text-primary` / `--color-text-body` / `--color-text-tertiary` / `--color-text-muted`). The CardForge `--aura-*` / `--mood-*` / `--glow-*` system is a different brand and does not apply here. Hover-glow tokens for warm-amber accents: `--color-accent-amber: #d4a952`, `--color-accent-amber-glow-near: rgba(212,169,82,.55)`, `--color-accent-amber-glow-far: rgba(212,169,82,.25)`. - **Pre-existing git repository gripe (not introduced this session, not blocking).** `fatal: bad tree object 192fa8ce30c23e8e33f7859ac635a664cbe6b9e6 / fatal: failed to run repack / error: task 'gc' failed` fires during auto-gc on every commit in the `ambientpixels/` working tree. Commits succeed regardless. Worth a `git fsck` + targeted repair pass in a dedicated session; not blocking deploys. ### 2026-04-21 - **Keep-alive pinger shipped — cold starts eliminated.** GitHub Actions cron (`.github/workflows/keepalive.yml`, `*/5 * * * *`) hits new unauth read-only `/api/healthz` every 5 min, then POSTs the result to authenticated `/api/keepalive-record`. The record endpoint appends a `{ts, latencyMs, status}` entry to a 100-entry ring buffer at state key `pingLog` — written via `_utils/companyStorage.js` directly, bypassing `company-state/index.js` so no `VALID_KEYS` entry was added (`pingLog` is NOT a valid `company-state` API key, only readable/writable via the two new dedicated endpoints). Dashboard surfaces status via new authenticated `/api/keepalive-status` (null-safe on empty log) rendered as a `KEEPALIVE` pill in the CEO status strip on `modules/company/dashboard.html` alongside HEARTBEAT/API/DEPLOY/AI MODEL/BUDGET/FLEET — green <6m, yellow 6–15m, red >15m or `status=fail`. Verified post-deploy: healthz warm latency 79–127ms (target was <500ms), round-trip record→status works, first cron fire green. **Auth caveat:** the `x-company-secret` gate on record/status is currently a no-op because `COMPANY_WRITE_SECRET` env var is unset on the function app (same state as every other authenticated endpoint — `storage.validateSecret('')` returns `true` when the env var is empty). Ring buffer cap of 100 bounds the flood blast radius. No alerting in v1; failures surface in Actions tab. Discord/Slack webhook is phase 2 if real failures occur. Cost: zero (GHA cron inside existing minutes, ~8,640 extra function invocations/mo inside Azure consumption free tier). ### 2026-04-15 (later) - **`activationMode` consolidated into `execution_mode`.** One autonomy dial now instead of two. `execution_mode` gained a `manual` value joining the existing `active | observe | frozen`: agents in manual mode propose + observe only, no task mutations, no memory writes. The redundant `activationMode` state key (which was never writable — not in VALID_KEYS — so always defaulted) has been fully removed: deleted `resolveActivationMode`, `_normalizeActivationMode`, `ALLOWED_MODES` from `helpers.js`/`constants.js`; swapped both manual-mode gate sites (task-mutation loop in `index.js`, remember handler in `agent-runner.js`) to check `executionMode === 'manual'`; collapsed the CEO Config dashboard's two-dropdown "Activation Mode + Automation Mode" panel into one "Execution Mode" dropdown with 4 values. Agent prompt GATE CHECKLIST rewritten to document `execution_mode` values. Experimental mode (the 1.5x rate-cap multiplier) retired — never wired in prod. N [... section truncated]

skills.content: # AmbientScore Development Skill AmbientScore is AmbientPixels' standalone AI website conversion audit product. Users enter a URL, get an instant 0-100 score with a letter grade, see 3 teaser findings for free, and can unlock the full report ($29 single / $89 3-pack). The product lives at `/ambientscore/` and is self-contained — its own CSS, JS, and API layer. ## Recent Changes _Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of AmbientScore and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block. Entries older than 30 days get condensed into the main skill body._ - **2026-06-11 — Codex audit: Claude migration is COMPLETE + monetization gaps.** The analysis pipeline runs on **Claude Sonnet 4** (`claude-sonnet-4-20250514`), not Gemini — the "Gemini analysis pipeline" wording in this skill's description and the "standing plan to switch" are outdated; the switch already happened. Cost: ~$0.04/scan (5 Claude calls: extraction, classification, 2 parallel dimension evals, synthesis). Checkout/webhook/credit-ledger/paywall verified working end-to-end. Gaps to fix (priority order): (1) no refund/dispute webhook handling — disputed customers keep report access; (2) unlock path doesn't verify the Stripe sessionId belongs to the requested reportId (metadata.reportId check missing in as-analyze); (3) no receipts/invoices beyond the summary email; (4) failed webhook = paid-but-locked report with no retry queue. Full audit: `ambientpixels/docs/system-codex/`. - **2026-04-21 — Editorial redesign landed.** The whole product moved off the dark emerald SaaS look to a formal editorial / filed-audit register. New palette (cream paper `#F3EEE3`, ink `#1A1613`, red stamp `#8C2F1E`), three typefaces (Source Serif 4, Inter, JetBrains Mono), bordered scorecards with ghost frames, mono dimension codes (`D-01 · MSG.CLR` through `D-08 · RSK.REV`), black grading-scale panel, signature block. Applies to landing, report (paywall + full), strategy intake, confirm. No em dashes anywhere in user-visible strings. All `as-*` classes and DOM ids kept so scan / paywall / credits / intake logic is unchanged. ## Architecture Overview ### Frontend Pages | Page | File | Purpose | |------|------|---------| | Landing | `ambientscore/index.html` + `js/ambientscore.js` | URL input, free scan results, upgrade CTA | | Report | `ambientscore/report.html` + `js/report.js` | Full report viewer with paywall logic | | Strategy | `ambientscore/strategy.html` + `js/strategy.js` | Lead capture intake form | | Confirm | `ambientscore/confirm.html` | Slot booking confirmation | ### API Endpoints | Endpoint | Method | Purpose | |----------|--------|---------| | `/api/as-analyze` | POST | Core scan — accepts `{ url }` or `{ sessionId }` (payment verification) | | `/api/as-report` | GET | Report retrieval — `?id=`, returns teaser or full based on unlock status | | `/api/as-credits` | POST | Credit check (`action: "check"`) or redemption (`action: "redeem"`) | | `/api/as-confirm` | POST | Strategy session confirmation with HMAC validation | | `/api/formIntake` | POST | Shared intake — type `"ambientscore_strategy"` for strategy submissions | ### Library Modules (`api/_lib/ambientScore/`) | Module | Role | |--------|------| | `analyzer.js` | Pipeline orchestrator — scrape → extract → classify → evaluate → score → synthesize | | `scraper.js` | URL fetching with SSRF protection, cheerio HTML parsing | | `dimensions.js` | 8-dimension model definition, weight profiles by site type, scoring helpers | | `promptBuilder.js` | Gemini prompt templates for each pipeline stage | | `scorer.js` | Deterministic scoring — decompression curve (1→0, 5→60, 10→100) | | `reportRenderer.js` | HTML report template generation | | `creditUtils.js` | Pack credit ledger (purchase/redeem history per email hash) | | `stripeClient.js` | Stripe checkout creation, session verification, webhook signatures | | `emailSender.js` | Azure Communication Services email delivery | ## The 8-Dimension Scoring Model The scoring model is the intellectual core of the product. It lives in `dimensions.js` and drives everything from prompt construction to report rendering. ### Group A — Conversion Funnel (55% base weight) 1. **Messaging Clarity** (15%) — Headline clarity, value prop specificity, jargon avoidance, consistency 2. **CTA Strength** (15%) — Visibility, action language, value alignment, placement 3. **Funnel Friction** (15%) — Step count, cognitive load, form optimization, distractions 4. **Conversion Hierarchy** (10%) — Visual hierarchy, information flow, progressive disclosure ### Group B — Trust & Differentiation (45% base weight) 5. **Trust Signals** (15%) — Social proof quality, authority markers, risk reversal, transparency 6. **Differentiation** (10%) — Unique mechanism, competitor contrast, category ownership 7. **Audience Alignment** (10%) — Language match, pain point addressing, sophistication calibration 8. **Quick-Win Fixes** (10%) — Low-hanging fruit count, implementation ease Each dimension has 3-4 sub-criteria. Gemini scores each sub-criterion 1-10, then the decompression curve maps LLM scores to 0-100 (because LLMs compress scores toward 5-7, a raw 5 maps to 60, not 50). Weights are dynamic — `dimensions.js` has profiles for SaaS, enterprise, ecommerce, content, media, local service, and agency site types. ### When modifying the scoring model - Adding a dimension: update `dimensions.js` (definition + weights for ALL site-type profiles), `promptBuilder.js` (evaluation prompts for the correct group), `scorer.js` (if weight math changes), and `reportRenderer.js` (display). - Changing weights: only touch `dimensions.js`. The scorer reads weights from there. - Changing the decompression curve: only touch `scorer.js`. The curve parameters are there. ## Analysis Pipeline (4 Stages) The pipeline in `analyzer.js` runs 4 Gemini calls (2 in parallel for Group A/B evaluation): **Stage 0 — Scraping** (`scraper.js`): Fetch URL, parse HTML with cheerio, extract headings, CTAs, forms, social proof, pricing, schema.org, body text. SSRF protection blocks localhost, private IPs, and cloud metadata endpoints. **Stage 1 — Extraction** (Gemini call #1): Parse scraped data into structured JSON — headlines, value props, CTAs, trust elements, audience signals, friction points, conversion paths. **Stage 1.5 — Classification** (Gemini call #2): Classify site type (SaaS, enterprise, ecommerce, etc.) to select the right weight profile. **Stage 2 — Evaluation** (2 parallel Gemini calls): Group A and Group B dimensions each get their own call. Returns 1-10 scores per sub-criterion + reasoning + findings. **Stage 3 — Scoring & Synthesis** (`scorer.js`): Apply decompression curve, compute weighted score, generate priorities, headline/CTA rewrites, confidence level. ### Pipeline development rules - Gemini prompts live in `promptBuilder.js` — keep prompt changes isolated there, not in `analyzer.js`. - The analyzer orchestrates; it should not contain prompt text or scoring logic. - Rate limiting (5 free scans/hour per IP) is enforced in `as-analyze/index.js`, not in the library. - Report data is stored as `cc_report_` in Azure Blob via `company-state` API. ## Monetization & Credits ### Stripe Flow 1. User clicks "Unlock" → `ambientscore.js` calls `/api/as-analyze` with just `{ url }` initially for free scan 2. For paid unlock → Stripe Checkout session created in `as-analyze/index.js` via `stripeClient.js` 3. After payment → redirect back with `sessionId` → `as-analyze` verifies payment and unlocks report 4. 3-pack purchase: 1 credit auto-redeemed for triggering report, 2 remaining ### Credit Ledger - Storage key: `cc_credits_` in Azure Blob - `creditUtils.js` manages the ledger: purchase entries, redeem entries, balance calculation - Credits are checked/redeemed via `/api/as-credits` endpoint - Frontend stores credit state in `sessionStorage` under `cc_pack_credits` ## Design System (Editorial Audit Report) AmbientScore's register is a formal filed-audit / financial document, not a SaaS landing page. Every visual decision is deliberate. Do not mix in SaaS tropes (gradients, glow, emoji, cards-with-shadows). ### Color tokens | Token | Hex | Usage | |-------|-----|-------| | `--paper` | `#F3EEE3` | Primary background (cream paper) | | `--paper-2` | `#EAE3D3` | Secondary bg (stats strip, dimension grid) | | `--paper-warm` | `#FBF7EB` | Dimension cells, warm panels | | `--rule` | `#D4CBB5` | Hairline rules, dotted borders | | `--rule-2` | `#BDB299` | Slightly darker rule | | `--ink` | `#1A1613` | Primary text, rules, buttons, dark panel bg | | `--ink-soft` | `#3D342C` | Body copy on cream | | `--ink-muted` | `#6B6052` | Meta labels, captions | | `--stamp` | `#8C2F1E` | Red editorial accent. Use sparingly: corner stamp, eyebrow rules, `›` caret, dimension codes, section eyebrows | | `--steel` | `#BFB5A0` | Muted text on dark panel (grading scale) | Body has two subtle radial gradients layered on cream to feel like paper, not a flat fill. Do not remove. ### Typography Three families loaded from Google Fonts (`` in every page head): - **Source Serif 4** — all headlines, giant grade letter (224px on hero sample, 200px on live scorecard), scorecard score, section headers, signature - **Inter** — body UI, button labels, form inputs (15–16px, weight 500–600) - **JetBrains Mono** — dimension codes, eyebrow labels, meta, uppercase chrome (10–11px, letter-spacing 0.14–0.22em) ### Emphasis rules (CRITICAL) Only three marks of emphasis. Nothing else: 1. **Italic serif** — editorial emphasis in headlines (`audit`, `method.`) 2. **Red stamp** (`--stamp`) — only: corner stamps, eyebrow rules, 36×2px red rule above quiet CTA, `›` caret before signature, dimension codes, section eyebrows 3. **All-caps JetBrains Mono** — codes, meta, ranges **Do not invent new emphasis mechanics.** No underlines, highlights, drop shadows, or color accents on body text. The restraint is the design. **No em dashes anywhere in user-visible strings** — use periods, colons, or the `›` caret. ### CSS conventions - **Prefix**: `as-*` for all classes - **Self-contained**: `ambientscore.css` has no dependencies on AmbientPixels framework - **Responsive**: Desktop-first. Breakpoints at `960px` (stack hero / method / dim / sig grids, collapse form layouts) and `560px` (stack remaining grids, collapse url-forms, smaller hero) - **Print styles**: hero / CTA / loading / decorative sections hidden; white background - Search `ambientscore.css` before creating new classes — reuse what exists ### Dimension codes (display contract) The JS maps dimension labels to the editorial codes shown in the UI. Keep this map in sync when dimension labels change in `api/_lib/ambientScore/dimensions.js`: | Label | Code | Short | |-------|------|-------| | Messaging clarity | D-01 | MSG.CLR | | CTA strength | D-02 | CTA.STR | | Trust signals | D-03 | TRS.SIG | | Funnel friction | D-04 | FNL.FRC | | Social proof | D-05 | SOC.PRF | | Offer clarity | D-06 | OFR.CLR | | Content flow / Continuity / Conversion hierarchy | D-07 | CNT.FLW | | Risk reversal / Differentiation / Quick-win fixes | D-08 | RSK.REV | The map lives as `DIM_CODES` at the top of both `ambientscore.js` and `report.js` (duplicated; update both). ## JavaScript Conventions - **Pattern**: IIFE (Immediately Invoked Function Expressions) — no module bundler, no framework - **DOM**: Vanilla `document.querySelector` / `innerHTML` — no jQuery, no React - **Security**: All user-facing strings go through `escapeHtml()` utility - **State**: Module-scoped variables (`currentReportId`, `currentUrl`) — no global state - **Error handling**: User-friendly inline error messages, not console-only ## Storage Keys | Key Pattern | Contents | |-------------|----------| | `cc_report_` | Full report JSON (score, dimensions, findings, rewrites) | | `cc_ratelimit` | IP-based rate limit tracking | | `cc_analytics` | Scan event analytics (90-day retention, 10K cap) | | `cc_credits_` | Credit purchase/redeem ledger | These use the `company-state` API with `x-company-secret: pixelpusher` header. The `cc_` prefix is a legacy from ConversionCore — do not rename (backward compat). ## Email Integration - Provider: Azure Communication Services (ACS) - Sender: `DoNotReply@ambientpixels.ai` - Template in `emailSender.js` — self-contained HTML safe for all email clients - Triggered after report unlock — sends full report summary to purchaser's email ## Security Considerations - **SSRF**: `scraper.js` blocks private IPs, localhost, and cloud metadata URLs before fetching - **Rate limiting**: 5 free scans/hour per IP in `as-analyze/index.js` - **HMAC**: Strategy confirmation uses HMAC token validation - **Anti-spam**: Form intake has honeypot field, minimum time-to-submit (2.5s), rate limiting - **Stripe webhooks**: Signature verification in `stripeClient.js` - Never bypass these protections — if they're in the way during development, ask the user ## Common Development Tasks ### Adding a new dimension 1. Define in `dimensions.js`: name, description, sub-criteria, weight in ALL site-type profiles 2. Add evaluation prompt in `promptBuilder.js` (assign to Group A or B) 3. Update `reportRenderer.js` to display the new dimension 4. Verify `scorer.js` picks it up (it reads from `dimensions.js` dynamically) ### Modifying report output - Report HTML template: `reportRenderer.js` - Report viewer (frontend): `report.html` + `report.js` - Report data structure: created in `analyzer.js` Stage 3 ### Changing pricing Current prices: **$29 single / $89 3-pack**. Change in all of the following when they move: - **Stripe** — price IDs in `api/_lib/ambientScore/stripeClient.js` + Stripe dashboard - **Landing CTAs** — `ambientscore/index.html` hero pricing line ("$29 full report with rewrites"), the quiet-CTA subtext ("$29 for the full report"), the stats-strip line ("Twenty-nine dollars for the full report") — note the stats strip is written out as words - **Landing buttons** — `ambientscore/js/ambientscore.js` → `buildFindingCard` / handleBuy has `'Unlock full report . $29'` as the reset label for the buy button. The HTML also has `$29` / `$89` in button labels - **Paywall** — `ambientscore/js/report.js` paywall render: `'Unlock full report . $29'` - **Masthead sub** — `index.html` mast-sub line "Issued on demand . 60 seconds . $0 to $29" - **Credit pack size** — `api/_lib/ambientScore/creditUtils.js` ### Adding a new API endpoint - Create `api/as-/index.js` + `function.json` - Add route in `staticwebapp.config.json` if needed (but be careful — that file has high blast radius) - Follow existing patterns: `x-company-secret` header check, try/catch with 500 response, JSON body parsing ## Future: Claude Migration There's a standing plan to switch from Gemini to Claude API for the analysis pipeline (better reasoning, more nuanced observations). Not yet active — the user said "not now." When AmbientScore analysis quality comes up, this option is worth mentioning.

# Blindspot Game — Development Skill

Use this skill when working on the Blindspot game — a standalone arena combat game at `/blindspot/`. Blindspot is fully independent from CardForge as of Mar 21, 2026 — zero shared CSS, JS, images, or audio. APIs forked but card save remains shared (product-agnostic).

## Recent Changes

_Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of Blindspot and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block. Entries older than 30 days get condensed into the main skill body._

### 2026-06-11 — Codex audit: monetization status confirmed

Full-product audit (see `ambientpixels/docs/system-codex/`). Confirmed: **Blindspot has zero real-money path** — no Stripe code, no checkout endpoint, no entitlements. The entire economy is Sparks soft currency (earned 3–25/battle, spent 10–200/item; Ember Crate at 50 Sparks is the only "paid" item). Wishlist (max 5) and loyalty milestones (250/500/1000/2500/5000 lifetime Sparks) exist but grant no rewards yet. Retention systems are the strongest in the portfolio (streaks, crates, daily bounties, PvP Elo, 26 cosmetics, 9 card titles). Path to first revenue: ~3–5 days via the existing `api/_lib/stripe/` pattern (Sparks packs or cosmetic packs) — recommendation stands to wait for 50–100 DAU before adding payment overhead. Scaling note: leaderboard/stats endpoints do O(N) blob aggregation per cache miss — precompute caches before ~500+ players.

### 2026-05-09 — Player leaderboard + public profile pages + editable display name (5 commits, range `c289c4e1a..37d35fad0`)

Big social-expansion session. Read this whole entry before touching `bs-leaderboard.js`, `profile-page.js`, the new `/api/blindspotleaderboard` or `/api/blindspotprofileview` endpoints, the Fighter Profile name editor in `renderStatsScreen` / `bindFighterProfileNameEdit`, or anything in the lobby card-actions / bounty progress / loot-zone / campaign-current-boss CSS scope.

**May 2 UI review polish closed** (commit `c289c4e1a`)
- **#10 Daily Bounties** — Progress strip moved from a 2px hairline to a 5px full-width bar at the bottom of each row. Empty-track strip behind it (`::after`, alpha 0.14) so partial-progress rows clearly read "ready to fill" instead of looking like a flat line. Reward label promoted to a real pill chip (gold-tinted bg + border, white-space nowrap, transition on transform). On done state the chip pops to success-green with `transform: scale(1.06)` + soft glow + bold weight.
- **#5 Forge/Save/Share buttons** — `.blindspot-lobby__card-actions .blindspot-btn` scoped rule: warmer gradient bg (gold tint), gold-dim border, taller padding (`1.05em 1.6em` vs the base `0.95em 2em`), gold-tinted icons, hover lift `-1px` + gold-glow drop-shadow + inner gold rim. Ghost variant kept for Share. Wired the orphaned `bs-forge-pulse` keyframe to `.bs-forge-progress--ready` so the forge tile breathes when the player can actually open it.
- **#7 Loot Zone hover** — Bumped `-2px` → `-5px` lift + `1.012× scale` on `.bs-loot-zone__row >` children. Layered drop-shadow (28px gold halo + black depth shadow + inner gold rim). Scoped to that direct-child selector so other surfaces using the same components keep their original hovers. Locked tiles + `prefers-reduced-motion` explicitly suppressed.
- **#4 Active campaign boss highlight** — Pure-CSS "NEXT UP" gold pill via `::after` on `#bs-boss-ladder > .bs-boss-card--current`. Pinned top-left over the avatar with a 2.4s breath animation. Ties the active ladder tile to the "Fight Next Boss" CTA above so the eye lands on it instantly. The campaign-screen pulse + gradient at line 14533+ already handles the rest.

**Bounty progress bar visibility fix** (commit `dfc1324d5`)
- First pass on #10 used `width: calc(100% - 1.2rem)` with a `0.6rem` left inset — the math clipped done bars to ~75% width, AND the empty-track alpha (0.04) was too dim to be visible on partial rows. CEO flagged it: "the gold bar is not filling like you describe."
- Simplified: bar fills edge-to-edge (`left: 0; width: var(--bounty-pct, 0%)`), height bumped 4px → 5px, empty-track alpha 0.04 → 0.14. Done bars now reach all the way across the row. Partial bars (`33%`, `50%`) are immediately readable.

**Player-based leaderboard with metric tabs** (commit `a7e260063`)
- The card-based leaderboard was hitting `cardforgeloadcards` (the same heavy 73MB / 8+ second cold-start endpoint we routed around for the splash slot machine on May 7) and timing out, surfacing as *"Could not load leaderboard. Try again later."*
- New endpoint **`GET /api/blindspotleaderboard?sortBy=wins|bosses|elo|power`** ([api/blindspotleaderboard/index.js](ambientpixels/api/blindspotleaderboard/index.js)). Reads profiles + `published-cards.json` directly. Returns top 50 ranked by the requested metric. Cache keyed by sortBy with 10-min TTL. Stale-cache fallback on aggregation error so a transient blob hiccup never blanks the board.
- Sort metrics:
  - `wins` (default) — `totalWins * 100 + min(99, bestStreak)`. Streak tie-breaks two players at the same win count.
  - `bosses` — `highestBoss * 1000 + ascension * 100 + min(99, totalWins)`. Asc-3 player ranks above asc-0 player at same boss count.
  - `elo` — `pvpElo` (current rating, NOT peak). Display shows current + peakRank label.
  - `power` — featured card combat-stat sum. Players with no featured card get 0 and naturally drop off.
- Server filters out profiles with `isDemo: true` and zero-activity profiles (`totalWins === 0 && highestBoss === 0 && pvpRecord.w === 0 && pvpRecord.l === 0`) so registered-but-unplayed accounts never list.
- Display name fallback chain (matched verbatim by `/api/blindspotprofileview`):
  ```
  profile.displayName       (player-set override — see name editor below)
  → publishedByName         (Google/B2C "name" auth claim from published cards)
  → 'Fighter ' + userIdShort
  ```
- `bs-leaderboard.js` rewritten end-to-end. New IIFE renders 4 tabs (Wins / Bosses / PvP Elo / Power) above a list of player rows. Each row: rank/medal + 56px circular avatar + display name + featured card chip + primary metric on the right. Avatar honors the player's saved `profileImageTransform` crop (`object-position` + `transform: scale`). Profiles without a profile image fall back to featured card avatar, then `fa-user-shield` silhouette.
- `setCallbacks` accepts `getUserId` so the visitor's own row gets the gold "(you)" highlight + border. Auto-binds tab clicks once via `_tabsBound` flag — repeat `render()` calls don't stack handlers. Captures `_activeTab` at fetch start so a fast tab switch doesn't render stale data.
- Each row is a full `<a href="/blindspot/profile.html?u={userId}">` link to the public profile page. CSS resets link chrome (`text-decoration: none; color: inherit`).
- Top 3 rows get gold avatar borders + crown/silver/bronze medals.

**Public profile pages at `/blindspot/profile.html?u={userId}`** (commit `586953e21`)
- Two-page architecture, deliberate. Public profile page is **view-only**, shareable, works unauthed. The in-game Fighter Profile screen (top-right dropdown → `#bs-screen-stats`) is the **self-edit** surface. Don't merge them — different audiences, different security postures, mirrors how Twitter / GitHub / LinkedIn split public profiles from settings.
- New endpoint **`GET /api/blindspotprofileview?userId={id}`** ([api/blindspotprofileview/index.js](ambientpixels/api/blindspotprofileview/index.js)). Hard read-only allowlist sanitization of the profile blob — never accidentally exposes auth-only fields. Distinct from `/api/blindspotprofile` (auth-scoped to caller, exposes consumables / equipped slots / claimedRewards / defenseCardId / lockedCards). Cache 5 min per userId, stale-cache fallback on errors.
- Sanitized response: `userId, userIdShort, displayName, displayNameIsCustom, profileImage, profileImageTransform, level, tier, tierLabel, xp, xpToNext, totalWins, bestStreak, highestBoss, ascension, towerBest, pvpElo, peakRank, pvpRecord, cardTitle, selectedCardId, createdAt, lastPlayedAt, cardsForged, cardsPublished, milestones[], featuredCard{}`.
- Explicitly excluded: email, real name beyond the `publishedByName` claim, charms / crates / cosmetic inventory, claimedRewards, bossRecords (per-boss W/L granular), masteryClaimed, defenseCardId, lockedCards, activeWagers, equipped cosmetic slots, campaign loss count.
- Returns `404 { ok: false, error: 'not_found' }` if profile blob doesn't exist or `isDemo === true`. UserId path traversal blocked via `/[\/\\\.]/` regex reject.
- `MILESTONES` list at the top of the endpoint mirrors `BsConst.CARD_TITLE_MILESTONES`. Same 9 entries (Blooded / Proven / Veteran / Champion / Legend / Hot Streak / Unstoppable / Boss Slayer / Conqueror). Keep in sync — server is the canonical computer of `earned: true|false`.
- `LEVEL_TIERS` mirrored too (Initiate → Apprentice → Veteran → Champion → Legend → Mythic). XP per level: 50.
- Featured card resolution: read selectedCardId from profile, lookup in `published-cards.json` (already opened for the displayName chain — no extra fetch). Slim payload sent: `{id, name, class, quote, rarity, avatar, combatStats, design, imageContainer, element, publishedByName}`.
- New page **`/blindspot/profile.html`** (with `/blindspot/css/blindspot-profile.css` + `/blindspot/js/profile-page.js`). robots ALLOWED on this page so OG previews work — sanitization makes it safe. `<meta name="robots" content="...">` is NOT set; defaults to indexable.
- Page composition: topbar (back-to-leaderboard + brand) → loading state → not-found / error states → hero strip (110px round avatar + name + Lv/Tier/Prestige + Peak Rank badge + highest earned milestone badge + "(this is you)" badge for visitor) → 6-tile record grid (Wins, Best Streak, Bosses, Ascension, PvP Record, PvP Win %) → featured card showcase (slim chip with avatar + stat bars + power readout + flavor quote — NOT the full BsCardRenderer) → 9-milestone grid (locked dimmed) → meta strip (Member since · Active Xago · forged + published counts) → CTA row.
- **CTA varies by visitor:**
  - Owner (visitor's userId === profile userId) → "Edit your profile" (deep-link `/blindspot/play.html#stats`) + "Copy share link" (clipboard).
  - Authed but not owner → "View Leaderboard" + "Copy share link".
  - Unauthed → "Forge your own card" → splash + "View Leaderboard".
- OG / Twitter meta tags injected at runtime once the profile loads. `og:title` = `{displayName} — Blindspot`. `og:description` = `Lv N {Tier} · X wins · Y/10 bosses · Peak {Rank}{ · Asc N}`. `og:image` = profile image OR featured card avatar OR `/blindspot/img/og-blindspot.png` fallback.
- `/.auth/me` fetched opportunistically alongside the profile fetch via `Promise.all` — purely for the "(this is you)" badge + Edit CTA. Failure is non-fatal; page renders identically without it.
- Featured card render is intentionally a slim chip (avatar + name + class + 5 stat bars + power) instead of the full `BsCardRenderer.renderCardHTML`. Loading the full renderer requires `bs-constants.js` + `bs-cosmetics.js` + ~5 other modules — too much weight for a public page. Stretch upgrade later if needed.
- Stat bar divisor auto-detect: if any stat > 20 → divisor 100; else 20. Same heuristic as `bs-card-renderer.js`. Prevents 0-100 CardForge editor stats and legacy 0-20 stats from rendering with the wrong scale.

**Editable display name + `#stats` deep-link** (commit `37d35fad0`)
- Two-page architecture cleanup. The "Edit your profile" CTA on `profile.html` was sending the player to `/blindspot/play.html` (lobby), not to the Fighter Profile screen. Fixed via hash routing.
- **Hash deep-links on play.html** — `initPlay()` now honors `window.location.hash` after the loading gate dismisses. Recognized hashes: `#stats` (Fighter Profile), `#leaderboard`, `#pvp`, `#shop`, `#collection`. The hash is stripped via `history.replaceState` post-dispatch so browser back / refresh don't re-trigger it. The block is wrapped in try/catch — failure is non-fatal.
- **Editable display name** — adds optional `displayName` field to the profile blob (default empty string). Players can override their auth-claim name without re-authing under a different account. Privacy escape hatch — Google / B2C `name` claim is the player's full real name for many sign-up flows, and it was showing on the public leaderboard.
- New **`POST /api/blindspotprofile`** action: `setDisplayName`. Validation: 2-24 chars (after `trim()` + internal whitespace collapse), permissive charset `/^[A-Za-z0-9 _'\-\.]+$/`. Allows real names ("D'Arcy", "Anne-Marie") AND gamer-tag patterns ("xX_Reaper_Xx"). Empty string is valid — clears the override. Server responds `{ success: true, displayName: trimmed }`.
- Server is the canonical validator. Client UI mirrors the same rules (`bindFighterProfileNameEdit` in `blindspot-flow.js`) but server NEVER trusts client validation. No profanity filter v1 — admin moderation panel exists for offensive names. No uniqueness — userId is the actual identifier, two players can both pick "Reaper".
- Display name fallback chain (used by leaderboard + profileview + Fighter Profile hero + bs-auth-ui topbar):
  ```
  profile.displayName       (player-set override)
  → publishedByName         (Google/B2C "name" claim from any of their published cards)
  → email username          (topbar fallback)
  → 'Fighter ' + userIdShort
  ```
- **Inline name edit UI** on the Fighter Profile hero — pencil button (`#bs-fp-name-edit-btn`) next to the name. Click → swaps the name out for an inline form (`#bs-fp-name-edit-form`) with input + save (✓) + cancel (×) + hint line. Pencil hidden for guests / unauthed (server POST would 401 anyway).
- New helper `bindFighterProfileNameEdit(currentName)` in `blindspot-flow.js`. Idempotent — uses `.onclick` / `.onsubmit` (not `addEventListener`) so repeat `renderStatsScreen()` calls don't stack handlers. Esc on the input closes the form. Hint text turns red on validation error.
- After save, `_profile.displayName` is mirrored locally + `BsAuthUI.update()` is called so the topbar chip + dropdown header pick up the new name without a reload. Lobby greeting (`#bs-lobby-username`) updates inside `BsAuthUI.update()`.
- `bs-auth-ui.js` `updatePlayAuthUI` now reads a `getDisplayNameOverride` callback (wired in flow.js's `_Au.setCallbacks`) FIRST before falling back to `userDetails.split('@')[0]`. So the override propagates to the topbar chip + dropdown header + lobby greeting consistently.
- `blindspotprofileview` exposes `displayNameIsCustom: true|false` for future UI (e.g. "set by player" tag).

**Watch list / pitfalls**
- **The two-page split is deliberate.** `/blindspot/profile.html` (public, view-only) vs the `#bs-screen-stats` Fighter Profile (in-game, self-edit). Don't merge them. Different audiences. Different security postures. The Fighter Profile section reads `_profile` from closure; profile.html receives a sanitized payload from the dedicated endpoint.
- **`/api/blindspotprofileview` is an explicit allowlist.** Don't `delete` from a spread — it's too easy to miss a new auth-only field added to the profile schema later. If you add a field to the profile blob and want it on the public profile page, add it to `sanitizeProfile()`'s explicit return shape. Otherwise it stays hidden.
- **`/api/blindspotleaderboard` cache TTL is 10 minutes per Function instance, keyed by sortBy.** After a player edits their displayName, leaderboard rows can lag up to 10 minutes. Same pattern as `blindspotstats`. Restart the Function App to force fresh aggregation; otherwise wait the TTL.
- **`/api/blindspotprofileview` cache TTL is 5 minutes per userId.** Same lag for the public profile page. The owner's OWN Fighter Profile in play.html updates instantly because it reads `_profile` directly, not the cached endpoint.
- **The MILESTONES + LEVEL_TIERS in `blindspotprofileview/index.js` are duplicates of `BsConst.CARD_TITLE_MILESTONES` and `BsState.LEVEL_TIERS`.** Server can't reach into client constants. Keep them in sync or refactor to a shared `_data/blindspot-meta.json` someday.
- **Leaderboard rows are anchors, not divs.** `.bs-lb-row` was changed from `<div>` to `<a>` so each row links to the profile page. CSS adds `text-decoration: none; color: inherit; cursor: pointer`. If you reorganize the row markup, keep it as a single anchor — nested interactive elements break accessibility.
- **Display name fallback is in 3 places, all must agree:**
  1. `bs-auth-ui.js updatePlayAuthUI` (topbar + lobby greeting)
  2. `blindspot-flow.js renderFighterProfileHero` (Fighter Profile name)
  3. `/api/blindspotleaderboard` + `/api/blindspotprofileview` (server-side render)

  If you change the order in one, change all three. The chain is `displayName → publishedByName → emailPrefix → "Fighter XXX"`.
- **The leaderboard endpoint runs `aggregate()` per cache miss = O(N) blob reads per Function cold start.** At ~7 active players that's fine. At >2000 players it becomes a heartbeat-precomputed `blindspot/leaderboard-cache.json` job. Same scaling note as `blindspotstats`.
- **`#stats` deep-link only fires once per page load.** The hash is stripped after dispatch. If you navigate WITHIN the page (e.g. user clicks "Manage Deck" then goes back to the lobby), they don't re-land on Fighter Profile. That's intentional — deep-link is for inbound navigation, not an in-app router.
- **Display name validation is permissive on purpose.** Single quote, period, hyphen, underscore, space, alphanumerics. Don't tighten without discussing — real names use these (`D'Arcy`, `Anne-Marie`, `Mr. Smith`). Profanity filter is an admin-moderation problem, not a regex problem.
- **Empty `displayName` is valid AND meaningful.** It clears the override, falling back to `publishedByName`. Don't reject empty strings or treat them as "no change." The validator branches: empty → accept; otherwise length + charset checks.
- **`_profile.displayName` may not exist on profile blobs created before the displayName feature.** All read paths use `(typeof p.displayName === 'string' && p.displayName.trim()) ? ... : ...` — never assume the field is present. The default-profile factory writes `displayName: ''` on new profiles, but old blobs keep their original shape until the next save.
- **`BsAuthUI.update()` re-runs the entire `/.auth/me` fetch on every call.** Calling it after every name save is fine (one fetch per edit) but don't call it in a hot loop. The fetch is cached server-side (Static Web Apps) but client-side it fires every time.
- **Bounty progress bar's `--bounty-pct` is set INLINE via `style="--bounty-pct:Npct"` in the JS render.** If you reach for a JS-set CSS variable without that inline pattern (e.g. setting `style.setProperty` on the element later), the in-row strip won't react. Pattern stays in sync because both render paths share `bs-rewards.js renderBounties`.
- **Loot Zone hover boost is scoped to `.bs-loot-zone__row >` direct children.** If you reuse `.bs-crate-opener` or `.bs-collection-panel` outside the lobby loot zone (e.g. an inventory page), it keeps the smaller original hover. That's deliberate. If you want the boosted hover elsewhere, copy the rule, don't widen the selector.
- **Campaign "NEXT UP" pill anchors via `position: absolute` on `.bs-boss-card--current::after`.** The parent `#bs-boss-ladder > .bs-boss-card` already has `position: relative` (line 1958). If you ever flip `.bs-boss-card` to `display: contents` or change the positioning, the pill will fly to the body root.

### 2026-05-07 — Publish-flow gap closed + public stats dashboard shipped (15 commits, range `c2489a676..89b56190d`)

Two distinct features shipped end-to-end. Read this whole entry before touching `bs-save-card.js`, `blindspot-quick-build.js` Step 5 (Become), `bs-battle-results.js` victory path, the `/api/blindspotstats` endpoint, the new `/blindspot/stats.html` pag

# CardForge Development Reference

CardForge is a browser-based RPG card creator with 40M+ visual combinations, AI generation, deck building, and a public gallery. It's a **pure card creator** — the arena battle system was removed in April 2026 (Blindspot handles combat). It runs as a static frontend on Azure Static Web Apps with Azure Functions APIs and Azure Blob storage.

## Recent Changes

_Changelog maintained by CEO. Agents should read this first — it reflects the most recent state of CardForge and may contradict older sections below. The sync script pulls this section to the top of every injected skill block. Entries older than 30 days get condensed into the main skill body._

### 2026-06-11 — Codex audit: monetization enforcement drift

Full-product audit (see `ambientpixels/docs/system-codex/`). Stripe is LIVE (cf-pro monthly $4.99/yearly, checkout + webhook + billing portal all working). But two of the three Pro flags are NOT enforced:
- **`premiumEffects` is a no-op** — the EffectTiers shim in `config.js` (replacement for the removed effect-tiers.js) returns ALL effects/borders unlocked for ALL users. Restoring gating means a real EffectTiers that checks `window.Entitlements.hasFlag('premiumEffects')`. 5 finished border PNGs (frost, ember, shadow, nature, circuit) exist but are unwired.
- **`extraCardSlots` is unused** — there is no draft card limit at all; the API accepts unlimited cards per user.
- Enforced and working: AI generation cap (free 5/24h vs Pro unlimited) and HD export (Pro 2x+).
- One-time products (effect packs, XP boosters) are commented-out stubs in `productCatalog.js`.
- Legacy arena HTML still renders in `cardforge-lightbox.js` (arena-record section) and `card-forge-editor.js` retains ~10 dead `combatStats` refs — cosmetic-only, but misleading; clean up when touching those files.

### 2026-04-25 — My Forge dashboard (cardforge/forge.html)

Top-level entry point that surfaces a signed-in user's drafts, published cards, favorites, and decks (saved + published) on a single page, replacing the multi-step "open editor → open right sidebar → pick tab" navigation. Linked from the global nav as **Forge** between Decks and the auth chrome.

**Page:** [cardforge/forge.html](ambientpixels/cardforge/forge.html) — placeholder header (`<header data-cf-nav="forge"></header>`), hero, anon CTA, 2x2 panel grid (My Cards, My Published Cards, My Favorites — top row; My Decks wide panel — bottom row, splitting Saved + Published side-by-side).

**Orchestrator:** [cardforge-forge-page.js](ambientpixels/cardforge/js/cardforge-forge-page.js) — `await window._cfPrincipalReady` (cached by cardforge-nav.js, no second `/.auth/me` round-trip), toggle anon CTA vs grid, mount/trigger panels.

**Reuse map:**
| Panel | How it mounts |
|---|---|
| My Cards (drafts) | `window.CardForgeMyCards.mount(container)` — new mountable module ([cardforge-my-cards.js](ambientpixels/cardforge/js/cardforge-my-cards.js)) patterned on my-published-cards |
| My Published Cards | **Auto-binds** to `#cf-mpc-list` + hidden `<button class="forge-sidebar-tab" data-forge-tab="published">` proxy; orchestrator clicks the proxy on init to trigger lazy-load |
| My Favorites | Same auto-bind pattern via `#cf-fav-list` + hidden `data-forge-tab="favorites"` proxy |
| My Saved Decks | `window.CardForgeMySavedDecks.mount(#cf-msd-grid)` — pre-existing generic mount API |
| My Published Decks | `window.CardForgeMyPublishedDecks.mount(#cf-mpd-grid)` — pre-existing generic mount API |

**Critical pitfall — module mount API asymmetry:**
- `cardforge-my-saved-decks.js` and `cardforge-my-published-decks.js` expose **proper `mount(container)` APIs** — they're generic, drop-in.
- `cardforge-my-published-cards.js` and `cardforge-my-favorites.js` do **NOT** expose `mount()`. They auto-bind on DOMContentLoaded to hardcoded editor sidebar selectors (`#cf-mpc-list`, `.forge-sidebar-tab[data-forge-tab="published"]`, `.forge-tab-content[data-forge-content="published"].active`, etc.) and lazy-load on tab click.
- Forge page works around this by **mirroring the editor's selector skeleton** (hidden `<button class="forge-sidebar-tab">` proxies + `<div class="forge-tab-content active">` wrappers) so the modules find their elements, then JS-clicking the proxies in `cardforge-forge-page.js` to fire the lazy-load.
- **Don't refactor either card module without auditing both consumers** — editor sidebar AND forge page both rely on the auto-bind. If you give them a `mount()` API, retain backward compat or update both pages in lockstep.

**Page-specific CSS:** [cardforge-forge.css](ambientpixels/cardforge/css/cardforge-forge.css) holds page layout + brings forward the `.cf-mpc-row` / `.my-cards-empty` row styles (from cardforge-ui.css#5054, scoped under `.cf-forge`) so the page doesn't have to load the entire 5000+ line editor stylesheet just for four panels.

**CSS/asset dependencies on the page:** `cardforge-base` + card render chain (card / bg-effects / border-effects / glow-effects / icons) + `cardforge-ui-components` (forge-action-btn, mini-card-scaler, cf-mini-fallback) + `cardforge-splash` (nav chrome + global `.cf-nav-active` ember rule) + `cardforge-deck-builder` (db-mpd-grid + tile styles for the deck modules) + `cardforge-forge`.

**Editor sidebar deliberately unchanged.** Both surfaces co-exist; whether to slim the editor's right-sidebar tabs (My Cards / Published / Favorites / Deck Manager) is a follow-up decision once the dedicated page proves itself.

**`.cf-nav-active` rule moved from `cardforge-admin.css` → `cardforge-splash.css`** during this work so every page using the unified nav (gallery, decks, forge, faq, roadmap, admin, devlog) gets the ember active highlight, not just admin.

**Cache-bust suffix bumped to `v=20260425b` for cardforge-nav.js across all 8 consumer pages** (otherwise the new Forge link wouldn't surface until each page re-fetched the script). Splash CSS bumped to `v=20260425s` for the .cf-nav-active rule move.

**Editor exception — manual Forge link.** `editor.html` uses its own compact `cf-page-bar` (not the unified nav injector — the 3-col grid layout reserves only ~80px for the header), so it doesn't auto-pick up new entries from `LINKS` in cardforge-nav.js. The Forge link was added to `cf-page-bar__actions` by hand next to Decks, reusing the existing `cf-decks-link` class for styling. **When you add another nav slot to `LINKS`, remember to also patch `editor.html` manually** — it's the only consumer page that bypasses the injector.

**Subhead font pitfall (recurring).** `.cf-forge__sub` declared color/size but no `font-family`, and `body.cf-forge-page` had no font set either, so the subhead inherited the browser default and rendered in Times New Roman — same root cause as the deck.html nav font bug. Fixed by adding a `body.cf-forge-page` rule in `cardforge-forge.css` matching the splash body pattern (Inter + obsidian bg/text). Pattern to remember: **every new page-class body needs its own font-family rule** unless the page sits under `body.cf-splash`.

### 2026-04-25 — Auth-gated nav links (Decks + Forge hidden from anon)

Both Forge and Decks are now hidden from the nav for anonymous users. They render only when signed in.

**Reason:** Forge is 100% sign-in content (every panel needs a per-user collection). Decks looks public but [cardforge-deck-builder.js:451](ambientpixels/cardforge/js/cardforge-deck-builder.js#L451) explicitly filters out default/sample cards, so a true first-time anon clicking Decks lands on an empty wasteland with zero cards. The shareable-deck-URL path (`?deck=<shareId>`) bypasses the nav, so this gate doesn't break sharing.

**Final nav state:**
| Anon | Signed in |
|---|---|
| Gallery / Editor / Sign in | Gallery / Decks / Forge / Editor / [user dropdown] |

**Implementation:**
- `requireAuth: true` flag on the Decks + Forge entries in the `LINKS` registry of [cardforge-nav.js](ambientpixels/cardforge/js/cardforge-nav.js#L34).
- `renderLink()` adds `hidden` + `data-cf-require-auth` when `requireAuth && !readAuthHint()`.
- `readAuthHint()` reads `sessionStorage.cfAuthHint` synchronously — set by `loadPrincipal()` after `/.auth/me` confirms signed-in. **This is the FOUC fix:** any returning signed-in user paints the links visible on first frame because the hint persists across the session.
- The `loadPrincipal().then()` callback sets `gated[i].hidden = !signedIn` and writes/clears the hint accordingly.

**Editor cf-page-bar exception (manual):** editor.html doesn't use the unified nav injector, so the same gating was applied by hand:
- Tagged its Decks + Forge `<a>` elements with `data-cf-require-auth` + `hidden`.
- Added a small inline `<script>` immediately after `</header>` that reads `sessionStorage.cfAuthHint` synchronously and unhides for returning signed-in users (FOUC-free for the most common case).
- Extended the existing inline `checkAuth()` IIFE near the bottom of editor.html to flip the gated links + write/clear the same `cfAuthHint` based on `/.auth/me` truth.
- Pattern to remember: **whenever you add a new auth-gated nav slot, both `cardforge-nav.js LINKS` AND editor.html's inline IIFE need updating.**

**FOUC envelope:** the very first signed-in visit per session to ANY CardForge page does flash hidden→visible briefly because no hint exists yet. Every subsequent navigation in that session paints correctly. Acceptable trade-off; eliminating the first-flash would need either an HttpOnly-cookie-readable hint or a server-side render path.

### 2026-04-25 — Unified global header (cardforge-nav.js)

Single source of truth for the `cf-splash-nav` chrome across every CardForge page that uses it.

**Pattern:** any page drops `<header data-cf-nav="<active>"></header>` and loads `cardforge-nav.js`. The injector renders the canonical markup (brand → Gallery → Decks → Editor + auth-aware Sign in / avatar dropdown), highlights the active link, and wires the dropdown popover (click toggle + outside-click + Escape).

- `data-cf-nav` value (`gallery`, `decks`, `admin`, `faq`, `roadmap`, `devlog`, …) → applies `cf-nav-active` + `aria-current="page"` to the matching link.
- `data-cf-nav-extras="admin"` → renders the Admin link, hidden by default; flipped on after auth resolves IFF userId is in `ADMIN_USER_IDS`.
- Auth state cached at `window._cfPrincipal` + `window._cfPrincipalReady` (Promise) — other modules can `await window._cfPrincipalReady` instead of hitting `/.auth/me` again.
- Idempotent: re-mount is a no-op (sets `data-cf-nav-mounted="1"` on the header).

**Pages that use the placeholder:** index, gallery, admin, faq, roadmap, devlog, deck.

**Deliberate exceptions (do NOT convert):**
- `editor.html` keeps its `cf-page-bar` — compact bar fits the 3-col grid's 80px header height.
- `login.html` keeps the brand-only strip — no nav distractions during sign-in.

**Deck SPA refactor:** `cardforge-deck-builder.js`'s old `db-bar` brand + auth chrome was removed (was duplicated across 4 view modes). The global header now lives outside `#db-app` in deck.html so SPA re-renders below it don't disturb it. `db-bar` is now purely the deck builder's sub-nav (Builder / My Saved / My Published) + view-specific action buttons (Save, Publish, Copy Link, Clone).

**Devlog:** loads `cardforge-base.css` + `cardforge-splash.css` for the nav chrome while keeping `/css/base.css` + parent-site scripts for the body content (parent's `init-header-footer.js` still injects the footer at `#footer-container`).

**Pitfall — self-contained nav font:** the `.cf-splash-nav__links a` rule sets color/size/padding but NOT `font-family`. Splash, gallery, faq, roadmap have `body.cf-splash { font-family: Inter }` so links inherit Inter. Deck.html (and any future page that doesn't set body font) would inherit the browser default → **Times New Roman**. Fix: `.cf-splash-nav` itself now declares `font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif` so the nav is self-contained regardless of host page styling. Don't remove this without checking every consumer page.

**Files:** `cardforge/js/cardforge-nav.js` (~210 lines, idempotent IIFE). Removed duplicate `/.auth/me` + dropdown wiring from `cardforge-splash.js`, `cardforge-gallery-page.js`, `cardforge-admin-hero.js` (`renderNavAuth`), `cardforge-deck-builder.js` (`buildAuthMarkup` + `wireAuthBar`).

### 2026-04-25 — Admin KPI strip + favorites/hearts current state

**Admin KPI strip** (`api/cardforgeadminstats/` + `cardforge/admin.html` 4-tile grid):
- Admin-only `GET /api/cardforgeadminstats` returns `{ cardsPublished, users, hearts, favorites, computedAt, cacheAgeSeconds }`. 5-min in-memory cache per Function instance.
- Single enumeration over `user/` prefix yields Users (distinct prefixes) AND the favorites blob path list in one pass, then batches favorites downloads (50 in parallel). Hearts comes from summing `card-ratings.json`. Cards from `published-cards.json`.
- 4-tile responsive grid above the hero config form. `loadKpis()` is fire-and-forget from admin-hero init — KPI failure does NOT block the rest of the page.
- Auth: same `ADMIN_USER_IDS = ['5bb115c5-9077-4049-8af0-ce5085a9c315']` pattern as `cardforgeheroconfig`. Server gate is the source of truth (403 for non-admin). Endpoint accepts `x-ms-client-principal`, `x-cf-auth-principal`, or dev `X-User-ID` (non-prod only).
- Frontend uses `buildApiPath('adminStats')` (registered in `config.js apiEndpoints`). `setKpi(key, value)` applies `Number().toLocaleString()`.
- Phase 2 (deferred): weekly delta chips on each tile via `admin/stats-snapshots.json` written by a daily cron.

**Favorites system** — coupled with hearts, NOT separate endpoints:
- **Hybrid hearts:** anonymous users CAN heart (no idempotency, per-IP rate limit only — client tracks state in localStorage). Authenticated users get the "real" path: writing a heart also adds the card to their favorites blob, idempotent server-side.
- **Endpoints:**
  - `POST /api/cardforgerate` — body `{ cardId, action: 'add'|'remove' }`. Anonymous path increments aggregate count only. Auth path updates `user/{userId}/favorites.json` AND aggregate `card-ratings.json` together. Returns `{ cardId, count, hearted, idempotent? }`.
  - `GET /api/cardforgefavorites` — returns `{ cardIds: [], updatedAt }` for the authenticated user. Anonymous returns `{ cardIds: [] }` with status 200 (no 401 noise during boot).
  - `GET /api/cardforgeratings` — returns flattened `{ ratings: { cardId: count }, updatedAt }` for community display. 30s public cache.
- **Storage:**
  - `card-ratings.json` (root) — `{ ratings: { [cardId]: { count, updatedAt } }, updatedAt }`
  - `user/{userId}/favorites.json` — `{ cardIds: string[], version: 1, updatedAt }`
- **Caps:** `FAVORITES_HARD_CAP = 2000` per user. `add` past cap returns 409.
- **Frontend boot:** `CardForgeHearts.init()` is idempotent — call from any page that needs hearts/favorites state. Used by splash (highest-rated mode), gallery, and admin (KPI live preview).

**Auth flow (simple, current):**
1. Frontend calls `/.auth/me` (handles both `clientPrincipal` shapes — object or single-element array).
2. `window._cfGetAuthHeaders()` (in `config.js`) caches the principal and returns `{ 'X-CF-Auth-Principal': JSON.stringify(principal) }`.
3. Cross-origin POST/GET to `ambientpixels-nova-api.azurewebsites.net` go with `credentials: 'omit'` + that header (SWA does NOT proxy POSTs through `/api/*` rewrites — direct calls to the Function App are the canonical path).
4. Function `extractUserInfo(req, context)` reads, in order: `x-ms-client-principal` (SWA-injected, base64 JSON) → `x-cf-auth-principal` (custom forwarded JSON) → `x-ms-client-principal-id` → dev `X-User-ID` (non-prod only). Defaults to `{ userId: 'anonymous', isAuthenticated: false }`.
5. Admin gate is a hardcoded `ADMIN_USER_IDS` list inside each admin endpoint — NOT in SWA config. CSRF auto-injected on POST by `csrf-protection.js`.

**On deck — global header alignment:** the `cf-splash-nav` chrome (Gallery / Decks / Admin / Sign in / Open Editor) renders consistently on splash + gallery + admin, but other CardForge pages (editor, deck builder, login) still carry older nav variants. Next pass: factor a single header partial (or shared init that injects the nav) so every CardForge page gets identical chrome, active-link state, and auth-aware Sign in / user-status swap.

### 2026-04
- **Arena battle system removed.** CardForge is now a pure card creator. All arena endpoints, combat logic, and PvP references are gone. Blindspot handles combat as a standalone game. Do NOT reference arena features, battles, or PvP when writing about CardForge.

### 2026-04-24 — 3-panel obsidian redesign (massive)

The editor was rebuilt around a 3-column obsidian/ember design system. Big behavioral and structural changes — read this whole section before editing the editor or splash.

**Page split:**
- `cardforge/index.html` is now the **splash page** (hero card fan, 8-digit combo ticker, three ways-to-start tiles). Real cards loaded from `/api/cardforgeloadcards`. Empty fan until API resolves, then fade-in.
- `cardforge/editor.html` is the **editor** (formerly index.html). All script/link `?v=` cache-busts at `v=20260424i` after the redesign sprint.
- Splash → editor entry points: `?start=quick|preset|blank` (handled in cardforge-layout.js handleStartParam IIFE).

**3-column grid layout** (cardforge-layout.css):
```
.cf-app-grid: grid-template-columns: 220px minmax(520px, 1fr) 620px
              align-items: stretch; height: calc(100vh - 80px)
  .cf-rail        (col 1) — 12-entry workflow nav
  .cf-preview-pane (col 2) — card floats on obsidian background
  .cf-main-pane   (col 3) — controls (overflow-y: auto)
```
All three columns share a single row height. Rail can collapse to 64px via `body.cf-rail-collapsed`.

**12-entry rail nav with workflow groups** (editor.html):
- Groups: START / STYLE / CONTENT / SHIP
- Each `.step-btn` carries `data-nav-id` (string) + `data-target-section` (numeric) + optional `data-target-tier`. The numeric section maps to `[data-step-section="N"]` panes inside cf-main-pane.
- `data-target-section` 4 and 5 (buffs, attributes) live on the **back face** of the card; switching to those nav-ids auto-flips the card via `activate()`.

**CardForgeNav API** (cardforge-layout.js):
- `window.CardForgeNav.activate(btn, opts?)` — activates a rail button. `opts.suppressFlip: true` skips the auto-flip (used by click-to-edit on back-face zones).
- `window.CardForgeNav.activateById(id, opts?)` — same, by `data-nav-id`.

**Click-to-edit on both card faces** (cardforge-layout.js wireCardClickToEdit):
- One delegated click listener on the outer `.card-preview-canvas` wrapper covers both `.card-front` and `.card-back` (the JS render later adds the `.card-preview-canvas` class to the inner front/back divs too — DON'T re-attach listeners there).
- Zone selectors include front classes (`.card-name`, `.card-stats`, `.card-badges` etc) AND back classes (`.badges-container`, `.attributes-container`, `.biography-section`, `.back-header`, `.bio-read-more`).
- When `e.target.closest('.card-back')` is truthy, handler calls `activateById(id, { suppressFlip: true })` so the card stays on the back while the rail jumps to the appropriate editor.
